record: Official rule and metric excerpts used by this repository
verification_method: fetch_page tool read of the official pages listed below; excerpts copied verbatim from the returned text. The sandbox network allowlist does not include drivendata.org or docs.nlr.gov, so these excerpts were not re-fetched by a repository script.
evidence_class: OFFICIAL RULES / PUBLIC PAGE TEXT; NOT A SUBMISSION RECEIPT

claims.topic: Submission format (float32, [0,1], outside-bounds null/NaN, 100 m, EPSG 32611)
claims.quote: Your submission has the same bounds as the training data, and data outside the bounds is null or nan. Your submission contains a single layer with datatype of 32-bit float (`float32`) with values between 0 and 1 indicating the confidence or probability of fault presence, with higher values indicating higher probability.

Your submission is in the same projected coordinate reference system as the training data (projected coordinate system for UTM zone 11N, EPSG 32611). Your submission is at the same resolution as the training data (100m).

claims.topic: Distance-weighted Tversky index, alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel
claims.quote: For this competition, we set 𝛼=0.2 and 𝛽=0.8 ... the range 𝑅 is 300 meters (i.e., 3 pixels at 100m resolution).

claims.topic: Scored test labels are NOT the USGS catalogue
claims.quote: For this competition, the sponsors have compiled a set of newly identified faults in the GeoDAWN region that are not included in the existing USGS fault database. These new faults have been manually labeled by fault experts and comprise the test dataset for the competition.

claims.topic: Training labels are existing fault data
claims.quote: The training labels contain existing fault data at 100-m resolution where positively labeled pixels indicate fault presence.

claims.topic: Submissions per week and one final submission
claims.quote: each participating entity may submit more than one set of predictions for automated scoring on the competition platform up to three per week, as specified on the competition website. ... Each participating entity ... is allowed to have one final submission

claims.topic: Weekly cap wording in the process overview
claims.quote: subject to the limits specified on the competition website (three submissions per week).

claims.topic: Originality warranty (basis for the 'do not copy a previous submission' rule)
claims.quote: The competitor’s entire submission is an original work by the competitor and the competitor has not included third-party content

claims.topic: Generative-AI disclosure is required in the narrative
claims.quote: you must indicate in the narrative (not included in the word count) the extent to which, if any, you used generative AI technology and how you used it to develop your submission

claims.topic: Public leaderboard shows best public DW-Tversky
